preamble: Under the laryngeal theory, the Proto-Indo-European laryngeals became the vowel i in Indo-Iranian when they stood between consonants and had to carry a syllable, whereas Greek gives e, a, o and Latin, Germanic and Celtic give a: *ph₂tḗr 'father' > Sanskrit pitā́ but Greek πατήρ, Latin pater. The atlas symbol [h] stands in for the laryngeals (*h₂ in the examples below, reconstructed as a pharyngeal, velar or uvular fricative rather than a glottal [h]). The *h₁ cases (hitá-, janitṛ́) are filed under glottal_stop_to_i, since *h₁ is often reconstructed as [ʔ]. In Iranian the vowel is often lost instead (Avestan ptā beside pitar-).

examples.note: Via Proto-Indo-Iranian *pHtā́; interconsonantal *h₂ vocalized to i. Compare Greek πατήρ and Latin pater with a.
Past participle of tíṣṭhati 'stands'; cognate with Greek στατός and Latin status, which have a.
Compare Greek θυγάτηρ with a and Gathic Avestan dugədar- with ə.
